articles.title: Tool Icon Auditor for repository contributors
articles.text:
# Tool Icon Auditor for repository contributors

The Tool Icon Auditor is a separate local development app available in a TinyGPT source checkout. It is not a setting or built-in editor in the installed desktop release. Repository contributors can open the **Open Tool Icon Auditor.cmd** launcher after the checkout's desktop dependencies are installed.

## Refresh and review tools

Choose **Refresh latest tools** to read the current production source without closing the auditor. The catalog includes built-in, desktop, Coding agent, Work, connector and local plugin declarations, plus host-generated activities such as conversation optimization. **New tools** marks newly discovered entries for review. The refresh timestamp identifies a source snapshot, not a separately installed or packaged release.

Icons are rendered through the production icon resolver. Explicit per-tool mappings take precedence over family defaults. Browser actions without an individual mapping use the globe icon; selected browser actions can instead show a window, cursor, keyboard, mouse or camera. Connected extension tools default to the plug icon, while specific connector or local-plugin actions can have their own mappings. Historical bot-prefixed activity defaults to the bot icon. These visual choices do not change which actions are available or permitted. Running and completed labels preview host fallback text. Actual tool summaries and model-authored status text may vary.

## Record icon choices

Select a tool, paste a Solar Linear slug or choose an icon from the installed catalog, then select **Save replacement**. Choices are saved in the checkout's local change file and survive closing or refreshing the auditor. **Applied** means the current production icon matches a saved choice. **Pending changes** lists choices that still differ. **Recorded changes** retains all saved choices, including choices for retired tools.

**Copy update request** copies only pending choices for current editable tools. Paste that request into the development assistant when ready to apply the mappings. Recording a choice does not modify TinyGPT's production icons automatically. An already-applied choice is retained until explicitly removed.

## Scope and limitations

The auditor does not connect to accounts, inspect private account data or query live remote MCP tool catalogs. Dynamic families represent tools whose names are discovered at connection time; they do not prove that a particular account action is currently available. Some actions have separate result displays or no rendered toolchain row. The auditor marks these differences. It does not change permissions, run the represented actions, install missing services or grant account access.

articles.title: Getting started and navigating TinyGPT
articles.text:
# Getting started and navigating TinyGPT

TinyGPT is a desktop assistant with Chat, Work, a personal Bot, Projects, a Library and Scheduled tasks. Its capabilities depend on the selected model, installed runtimes, connected plugins and your permissions. An answer about a capability is not evidence that an action has happened.

## Welcome and first launch

New installations open a five-step **Welcome to TinyGPT** experience: **Your private AI companion for every idea**, **Ask anything, anytime.**, **Tailored to you**, **Meet your Bot**, and **More than just text**. Layered vibrant gradients and sparse UI mockups, matching the website's Meet TinyGPT artwork, sit beside a setup panel on desktop. The first screen offers **Light** and **Dark** appearance choices; these immediately preview and save the app theme. Keeping the existing theme needs no action. The panel starts below the window-control area, and its details scroll independently of navigation in short windows.

Artwork uses sample TinyGPT interface details; pictured prompts and memories are illustrations, not imported files, saved personal data or results of an action. The Bot artwork uses the app's animated avatar and respects Reduce motion. Artwork is decorative, excluded from assistive reading, and has no setup controls. There is no step count, brand dot or promotional footer note; progress dots remain beside navigation. Progress is saved on this computer and resumes after a restart. Earlier four-step progress on its final screen migrates to the new final screen; completed or skipped profiles remain completed or skipped. **Set up later** closes the welcome; reopen it through **Settings → General → Welcome to TinyGPT → Open welcome**. Existing profiles are not forced through setup. Reopening welcome preserves existing connections and permissions until you explicitly change a setting. Every setup choice is optional: use **Add later**, **Skip this step**, or **Set up later** without losing ordinary Chat access.

**Ask anything, anytime.** describes included on-device AI as **free forever**. The included model starts automatically; welcome has no included-model selection card. Optional extras show **TinyGPT Pro** only when the actual device check confirms Pro compatibility. **Set up** opens the existing Pro download/setup panel, including its download size, progress and cancellation. Merely viewing this step or choosing **Add later** does not download Pro. If optional Pro setup fails or is canceled while the included model remains selected, welcome attempts to restart the included model; it preserves a cloud selection made meanwhile. **OpenRouter**, with its logo, offers **Connect** for browser sign-in to your own account; usage may cost extra. Add these extras later in Configuration. No account, Pro setup or cloud connection is required to finish welcome. Included local AI works offline after required model setup; readiness and device compatibility still apply.

**Tailored to you** offers **Your first name (optional)**. Continuing with a new nonblank name saves it to the local profile and an explicit **Your name** personal memory, preserving any existing last name and other profile fields. Leaving it blank skips this choice and does not erase an existing name. Back, **Skip this step**, and Set up later do not save an edited name. A failed name save keeps setup on the same screen. On a new profile, providing your name opts into using personal memories; an existing memory-sharing choice, including an opt-out, is preserved. Manage the name in Profile and sharing, saved memories, Pause and Forget in Personalization. Other personal conversations are not automatically learned as memories.

**100% local storage** means your profile name and saved memories are stored on this computer. Relevant memory excerpts may still be sent with a request if you select a cloud model. This is a storage statement, not a claim that cloud inference is local or that memory is encrypted.

**Meet your Bot** shows the real animated avatar and offers **Set up now** or **Add later**. Set up now opens the existing Bot appearance and access flow. Complete that flow to create/configure the Bot, then return to the final welcome screen. Closing it returns to welcome; closing is blocked while the final Bot save is in progress. Add later does not prepare or configure a Bot, enable proactive checks, grant plugin access, or change permissions. The sidebar offers Bot setup afterward. An already configured Bot is shown as set up and is preserved.

**More than just text** introduces Work, coding, documents and voice. **Read replies aloud** changes the existing voice preference only after a successful save. Welcome does not request microphone access, enable computer control, connect plugins, or enable Remote Control. Permission prompts remain part of using those features. Conversations are saved locally, but cloud models receive the context sent to them. On the final screen, choosing a starter fills a new conversation draft when you select **Open TinyGPT**. It does not send a message automatically.

The public app and installer name is **TinyGPT**. Windows packaging targets x64 with a branded web setup wizard. New installer builds download the app package during setup and prepare separately stored included model data on first launch; matching installed models can be reused. Once model setup completes, included local AI and voice work offline. Signed Windows release builds support user-controlled updates through an indicator above the sidebar profile and **Settings → General → Updates**. Existing 0.1.0-prebeta.2 users need a manual installer upgrade once. See **Updating TinyGPT and keeping local models** for download, restart, storage and availability limits. Mac packaging targets Apple Silicon on macOS 15 or newer, but a Mac pre-beta download and updater are not currently offered. Signing, notarization and clean-machine acceptance are separate checks. Changing the public name preserves the existing app identity and local profile directory.

## Start a conversation

Open a new chat, choose Chat or Work in the composer, select an available model and send your request. Chat suits questions, research and everyday tool tasks. Work carries a task through file changes, commands and verification. Use Stop to interrupt an active reply. Retry or regenerate when appropriate; earlier tool actions may already have happened, so check their results before repeating them.

Use the sidebar to reopen conversations, find Projects, open your Bot, browse the Library or manage Scheduled tasks. Conversations and preferences are saved on this computer. Search chats to find older work. Archiving hides a conversation from the sidebar; Settings → Archived chats restores it. Deletion and archiving are different actions.

## Find a setting

Open Settings and type a label or related word in Search settings. Select a result to open its section and locate the control. Settings contains General, Configuration, Notifications, Profile, Appearance, Voice, Personalization, Computer use, Remote Control, Plugins, Browser, Work settings, Bot, Keyboard shortcuts, Archived chats and Diagnostics. A control may open another configuration panel.

On Windows use Ctrl; on macOS use Command. The shortcuts are modifier+J for New chat, modifier+B to toggle the sidebar, modifier+F to find in a conversation and modifier+K to search chats.

## Understand availability

TinyGPT supplies a small application-identity note and a snapshot of the computer's local date, time and timezone at the start of each reply or worker request chain. This helps Chat, Work, Bot and delegated coding interpret TinyGPT as their host app and phrases such as today or this week. The snapshot stays unchanged during tool follow-ups and retries, preserving a reusable prompt prefix. A new reply, resumed run or independent worker gets a fresh snapshot. It is labeled as reply-start time, not a live clock, so a long task may need to check the current time separately. It uses the desktop computer's clock and timezone; if a paired device is in another timezone, specify that timezone in your request. This context does not grant access or replace the Bot's name/personality, and it does not make the model's stored knowledge current news.

Choosing a more capable model does not grant file, browser or account access. A connected account still needs selection and authorization in the conversation. Device compatibility and available memory affect local models. If something is missing, check Configuration, the relevant plugin/runtime and General tool permissions. TinyGPT should report missing access instead of guessing or claiming success.

articles.title: Models, connections and offline use
articles.text:
# Models, connections and offline use

Open Settings → Configuration to choose and manage inference. Inference is the model that reads your request and produces a reply. TinyGPT includes local model setup and supports connected providers; available controls depend on the current build and device.

## Use built-in models

Find TinyGPT or TinyGPT Pro in Configuration and open its configuration panel. Use Check device and the displayed setup/status information before starting a model. Follow the panel's download or setup steps when needed. TinyGPT Pro is optional and requires a compatible device; it is not a guarantee that every computer can run it. Downloads and first-time preparation may need internet access.

The Configuration monitor shows graphics memory, system memory and supported GPU activity/temperature. Apple Silicon uses shared memory. Expand TinyGPT components to inspect allocations. High memory use can affect other applications. Keep local models loaded controls residency; Chat idle timeout controls when idle local chat and retrieval models release memory. A cold model may take longer to answer.

Pro's host prompt-snapshot budget adapts to available system RAM at startup. It can exceed 4 GiB to preserve a large Work prompt across image analysis, up to 16 GiB, while reserving 4 GiB plus half the remaining free RAM. This is a lazy host-memory limit, not a VRAM allocation. Low-memory machines may disable snapshots or still be unable to preserve a large state; numeric Diagnostics records show skipped snapshots when enabled. The model context window and configured output allowance are unchanged.

## Connect other models

Open Local models to discover models already served by Ollama, LM Studio or another compatible local server. That server must be running and configured appropriately. The current Configuration interface exposes built-in models, OpenRouter and Local models. Internal support for other provider protocols does not mean there is a visible sign-in/control for them in this interface. Choose a supported model and connection rather than assuming every model supports tools, images or reasoning. Effort controls affect reasoning only where the selected model supports it.

OpenRouter uses your connected account and credits. Model access selects free or broader model access. Cost tier affects Auto Router price ranges; higher tiers can cost more. Review the actual connection and model information before relying on cost assumptions. A consumer subscription to a different chat product does not itself establish API access in TinyGPT.

## Offline boundaries

Once required assets are installed, local inference, local handbook lookup and supported local transcription/retrieval can operate without a cloud inference account. Web research, remote connections, cloud models, connected accounts and downloads need their respective network services. A locally stored conversation can still send prompts and selected evidence to a cloud model when that connection is selected. Offline support does not mean every feature works without internet.

articles.title: Chat, research and answers
articles.text:
# Chat, research and answers

Use Chat for questions, writing, research and supported tool tasks. Choose a connection and model, type your request, and attach relevant material using the composer. The selected model's tool and image capabilities affect what it can do. With tools disabled, the assistant can answer from supplied context but cannot claim to have browsed, edited files or contacted an account.

## Research a question

Ask for web research when current sources are needed. Search and page reading can run in the background. Source chips and citations connect an answer to its evidence. Open the cited source to inspect it. A cited passage can be incomplete or outdated; a search result alone does not establish the truth of an entire answer.

Interactive website work uses TinyGPT's browser tools. The user can watch browser work. Sign-in, verification, consent and sensitive input may require a handoff in the same tab. Complete the requested step, then let the task resume. Browser settings select the search engine, link destinations and privacy controls.

## Follow a reply

Local-model loading appears in the conversation's working history with a square refresh icon.

A Chat reply has one tool chain, one temporary progress message below it, and one answer area. A new progress message replaces the previous one as it streams. Starting another tool keeps the latest progress message in that position; it does not become the chain’s title or get folded into the tool disclosure. Expand the chain to inspect tools and thinking. Once the harness identifies the final answer, the temporary progress message disappears and the answer appears in its own area. Progress does not return when the reply completes or is reopened.

Streaming follows the provider’s answer/progress signals. Built-in thinking models retain their answer-boundary validation, so their final text can remain held until the model finishes cleanly. Text without a confirmed answer signal can be shown as temporary progress before promotion. The layout does not guess finality from wording, remove model checks, change tool permissions or replay actions. Work retains its chronological working history and nested Coding agent sections.

An answer can begin with a generated visual, such as a comparison table or chart, before any final text. That also hides temporary progress, including while the visual is being prepared. A later tool-only visual does not turn an earlier research update into answer text. The same display rules apply in the mobile companion.

## Manage a conversation

Use available message controls to copy, regenerate or export an answer. Find in conversation locates text in the current conversation; Search chats finds saved conversations. Branching/retrying follows the selected conversation history. TinyGPT may summarize older context to fit the model's window while preserving saved original messages. That does not give the model unlimited recall of every past detail.

## Ask about TinyGPT

Bundled product help explains this installed build's behavior and settings. The assistant can search it with search_help, including by article ID to read a full topic. Product-help passages are separate from personal memories. Ask for clarification if a feature's availability depends on your model, operating system, connection or permission. The assistant must distinguish general capability from access verified in this conversation.

articles.title: Projects, files, attachments and outputs
articles.text:
# Projects, files, attachments and outputs

Create a Project to organize related conversations, provide Project instructions and optionally select a folder. A selected folder grants scoped access for supported file tools. Relative tool paths refer to that folder, or to the conversation's managed Generated files folder when no Project folder is selected. A folder grant does not authorize every possible write or command; General tool permissions still apply.

## Give the assistant a document

Use the composer attachment controls to select files or available saved sources, then ask a specific question about them. File processing must finish before content is usable. Text/code, supported documents, PDFs and images have different extraction paths and limits. Inspect any processing error rather than assuming an unreadable file was indexed. Image interpretation depends on available image tools/model support; omitted visual details are unknown. A model's visual observation can be wrong, especially for small text.

Supported document extraction includes text-layer PDFs, Word DOCX, PowerPoint PPTX, Excel XLSX and ODT. PDF pages without readable text can use local OCR within processing limits; partial OCR failures produce a notice, and unreadable text must not be treated as successfully extracted. Spreadsheet extraction includes worksheet/cell content, and slide extraction preserves slide labels. Complex formatting, drawings and visual layout may need separate inspection. Consult the original when extraction is partial.

Image and scanned-page OCR uses the bundled local English Tesseract engine. Repeated column whitespace can produce separate reading regions with original-image coordinates and confidence estimates. Multi-column recovery uses at most four targeted regions, a bounded pixel budget, and stops starting retries after its time budget. It preserves baseline text when numeric readings conflict or a retry fails, and flags uncertainty rather than silently correcting prices or counts. Region grouping is geometric, not proof of which semantic label owns a feature. No automatic cloud or vision-model request is added by OCR.

For uncertain image OCR, read_source returns the saved image reference and guidance to use view_image with a focused question. Visual inspection depends on model/tool access and may still be wrong; unresolved values must remain uncertain. A ready processing status is not an accuracy guarantee. Existing saved OCR is retained until the file is retried or uploaded again; updating the app does not silently reprocess all attachments.

Saved sources and extracted passages support cited retrieval within the applicable conversation/Project. An attachment to one conversation is not blanket access to unrelated personal chats or other Projects. Project folder indexing is managed separately in Personalization; newly granted Project folders are indexed automatically unless an existing setting has paused or disabled indexing.

## Find generated files

Successful file writes appear as file cards and in the Library. Open the Library to inspect outputs and available previews, and use the file's available save/export controls. Do not treat an answer saying 'saved' as sufficient if no successful file action occurred. A preview is not a complete verification of a document's contents.

Work can show changes, command results and guarded Undo. Inspect changes before undoing: later modifications can prevent a safe reversal. Deleting a chat, forgetting an index and deleting an original disk file are distinct operations. Forgetting indexed evidence does not remove the original file.

articles.title: Memory and local retrieval
articles.text:
# Memory and local retrieval

Open Settings → Personalization to manage saved memories, Project folders and Inspect retrieval. TinyGPT uses explicitly saved facts/preferences and indexed eligible content; it does not automatically index unrelated personal chats. Personal-memory sharing defaults on unless explicitly disabled. Project evidence stays within the corresponding Project.

## Save or change a memory

Choose Personal or a Project in Saved memories, select Add memory, enter a title and fact/preference, and save. Edit changes the text. Pause keeps a memory but removes it from retrieval; Enable restores it. Forget removes it and its derived retrieval evidence. Use personal memories controls whether saved personal facts are shared across conversations and Projects. Your profile name is saved as a personal memory when you provide it; manage that sharing here.

## Control folder indexing

Adding a folder to a Project starts indexing by default when no previous index preference exists. In Project folders, Refresh checks changes, Pause stops availability/indexing, and Enable indexing resumes it. Forget index removes indexed text and vectors, clears derived conversation checkpoints and turns indexing off. Original files and conversation messages remain. Forgetting an individual indexed file excludes it from later scans until its folder index is reset.

## Inspect what can be retrieved

Choose a scope in Inspect retrieval, enter a query and open a result to inspect its evidence. No results may mean the scope, sharing setting, file permissions or indexing state excludes the content. Local search combines keyword and semantic retrieval with relevance ranking. Bundled embedding/ranking models run on this computer; keyword search remains useful when inference is unavailable. Indexes are rebuildable search data, not the authoritative originals.

## Privacy and help

Memories and indexes are stored locally, but relevant excerpts can be sent to your chosen inference connection. Disabling sharing does not recall information already sent to a provider or erase original saved messages. Bundled TinyGPT help is a separate application-knowledge category; it remains available when personal-memory sharing is off and contains no personal account data.

articles.title: Work tasks and verification
articles.text:
# Work tasks and verification

Choose Work in the new-conversation composer for tasks that require concrete actions, files, commands and checking results. Select a Project folder when working on existing files; otherwise supported file actions use the conversation's managed output folder. Keep compatible tool support enabled in the selected connection.

## Complete a task

Describe the desired outcome, constraints and relevant files. Work can plan a substantial task, use available tools, request missing information, and report results. Approvals are handled by TinyGPT's permission controls. Review the actual approval card before allowing a change. Existing authorizations can apply to subsequent actions, but denied actions must not be bypassed through another interface.

Questions use compact option rows and a single-line custom answer field. Longer answers scroll within that field. Choose an option or type your own answer, then submit; Work continues the same task after the answer is saved. The question-circle icon identifies the question tool in the working history. Inline questions, permission requests and browser sign-in handoffs leave the workspace browser usable while the task waits. Stop task cancels the pending task instead of submitting an answer.

Commands take a program and separate arguments. Long-running jobs have status and stop controls; a started job is not a finished job. Commands run with operating-system permissions and are not a general OS filesystem sandbox. Do not assume selecting a Project prevents every effect of an approved program.

## Bundled Python, Node, npm and npx

Work commands, the Coding agent and workspace terminals use the same bundled Python 3.13.18, Node.js 24.22.2, and npm/npx 11.19.1. No separate system installation or first-run runtime download is needed. Python is available as both python and python3, with its standard library, SSL, SQLite, venv and python -m pip. Node runs as a standalone executable. TinyGPT places these tools before system installations on the command path and keeps package-manager configuration and caches separate from your usual user configuration. If bundled files are missing or invalid, TinyGPT reports an unavailable-tools error instead of silently selecting a system runtime. The desktop packages target Windows x64 and Apple Silicon macOS.

Install additional Python packages in a Project virtual environment: run python -m venv .venv, then use .venv/Scripts/python.exe on Windows or .venv/bin/python on macOS with -m pip. Package installation into the shared bundled Python is disabled by default. Each Project can keep its own packages without changing the Python used by other chats. npm and npx use the bundled Node; npm install and npm run work in the selected project. npx can run project-installed commands. Installing or downloading additional dependencies still uses the normal command permission controls and may require internet access. Offline use works for built-in libraries and dependencies already available locally; the bundle does not include every Python/JavaScript library, native compiler, Git, or other external program. Terminals can still run other installed system tools. These runtime choices do not restrict commands to an OS sandbox.

## Inspect results

Work’s working history shows prose, thinking and tools in their recorded order. Coding work appears inside an inline **Coding agent** section, containing its own updates and tools. It opens while active and collapses when that coding call ends; the assistant can continue reviewing afterward. The outer history collapses when the final answer is confirmed. This same presentation is used on the mobile companion with a bounded recent history that preserves the parent of retained coding tools. Mobile does not expose the full native session or raw tool results.

Review changed files, diffs, checks and command exit results. Work should verify outputs with tools and report material limitations. Guarded Undo checks whether reversal is safe; it cannot undo external messages, purchases or arbitrary command side effects. Stopping a task cancels ongoing work where supported but does not reverse completed actions.

Working-history icons distinguish file, browser, command, skill and planning actions. Individual action icons take precedence over a shared family icon. Plugin-provided skill actions can therefore use a different icon from TinyGPT's built-in skill tools. Icons describe activity; they do not establish account access or permission to execute a tool.

## Smaller changes and output limits

Work and the Coding agent save a small working result first, then improve it with focused edits. Each native write, edit or patch accepts at most 16 KiB of UTF-8 change text; finished files can be larger. Oversized changes are rejected before execution. Incomplete tool calls are never executed, and an interrupted response does not mean a file was saved. Commands still use OS permissions; this file-tool limit is not an OS sandbox.

When the Coding agent reaches its output limit, Work preserves its session ID and reports whether it ran out during thinking, tool preparation or an answer. A follow-up coding attempt automatically resumes that failed session when no other session is specified. Continue restores this recovery context from the selected conversation branch, keeping existing file changes and current permissions.

Two output-limit failures in the same runtime without a further recorded file change pause Work with an actionable message. Directory listings do not reset that safeguard. Review the saved changes, revise the instructions or select another effort/model, then Continue. This prevents repeated fresh attempts from consuming the model indefinitely; it does not guarantee that a local model can finish every task. The configured total output allowance is unchanged.

## Long tasks and local context processing

Each model request includes the active conversation context: instructions, tool definitions, user requests, earlier assistant reasoning/replies and tool outcomes. Input-token totals can therefore include substantial existing history. A local prompt cache holds temporary computed state for a matching token prefix; saved conversation history is separate. Changes to an earlier prefix, cache eviction or unavailable model state can require processing old input again. An input-token total alone does not tell you how many tokens were reused.

For declared local llama.cpp connections, Work explicitly requests prompt caching and native progress counters. Diagnostics distinguish cached tokens from newly processed tokens and record character counts by payload category and how many complete messages remain unchanged at the front. Character counts are not exact tokenizer counts or proof of a cache hit. These records contain counts, not prompts, reasoning text, URLs or credentials.

The shared date/time note is a reply-start snapshot. It stays unchanged throughout a tool loop and retries, rather than rewriting a clock in the leading system instructions for each call. A new reply or resumed run gets a fresh snapshot. Work's request-shape measurements run after this shared note is applied, so they describe the body actually sent to the provider. A stable prefix enables cache reuse; deliberate history edits, changed tool definitions or missing model state can still cause a cache miss.

For local OpenAI-compatible Work runs, callable tool definitions stay fixed throughout a run. A bounded set of common browser tools is selected at startup. Additional tools and connected-plugin actions are discovered through load_tools; their parameters arrive as conversation data and invoke_tool calls the selected action through the normal host validation and approval flow. Discovery does not replace earlier tools or grant permissions. Smaller context windows may discover some browser actions through this same interface. This policy applies to Work; Chat, Bot and other provider protocols retain their existing tool-loading behavior.

Large native file/command results and browser observations are bounded when first returned. Work's native text reader returns a contiguous page of up to 2,000 lines or 50 KiB, including its continuation instructions, without a second head/tail excerpt that could hide the middle of that page. Its offset is a 1-based line number and limit is a line count. Continue with the returned offset to read more, or use a narrower line range. Saved-observation offsets are character offsets in an earlier captured result, not line numbers or a fresh file read. Large command/browser results can still use bounded excerpts with exact saved observations available for retrieval.

Existing history stays unchanged while context capacity is healthy. Local Work cleanup starts when measured context pressure reaches about 85% of the input budget and targets about 60%, leaving space for further tools and replies. Older long completed reasoning and large observations are retired only if the batch can reach that lower target. Otherwise Pi's normal compaction creates a checkpoint before the next model request; small edits do not repeatedly rebuild the same large prefix. For older successful large write/edit actions, cleanup retires the call and its matching result together into an explicit historical execution note. Exact arguments and results remain in a scoped saved observation; archive notices are never inserted into the content or edit arguments of a historical tool call. Failed, pending and recent call/result pairs remain intact. Current instructions, user messages, successful outcomes and recent reasoning remain available. Signed reasoning and other providers do not use this local reasoning-retirement policy. Archiving can invalidate a cached prefix; it reduces context growth but does not guarantee cache reuse or a particular speedup.

When continuing an existing local Work chat, TinyGPT repairs older host-generated write/edit argument placeholders from the original native call on the selected session fork. It preserves the original session and other branches. This repairs model context; it does not rewrite already-created project files or erase earlier mistakes. Use current file reads before making further changes. Exact native history and scoped observation retrieval remain available, including after Continue.

With Diagnostics enabled, active local runs record supported NVIDIA GPU activity, memory, clocks, power, temperature and limiting states about every ten seconds. Device-wide readings are correlated with request IDs and timing; they do not establish that one request caused all GPU activity. Counts of other compute processes may omit graphics workloads or unavailable driver data. Other devices report unavailable counters. Sampling stops when local runs finish, Diagnostics is disabled, or records are cleared. App-managed model timing, generation rates, acceleration acceptance and skipped prompt snapshots are saved as numeric events, so they remain inspectable after the native log rotates. Records use existing local retention and are not automatically uploaded.

Settings → Work settings controls Work effort, shared file/read/write/command approval policies, diff markers and code font size. Effort availability depends on the selected model. Presentation or document creation also depends on available tools and formats; a task description alone does not install missing software or establish a successful export.

articles.title: Your Bot and Scheduled tasks
articles.text:
# Your Bot and Scheduled tasks

Your Bot is a persistent personal assistant with its own conversation, identity, appearance and behavior. Use its setup flow, then its name/avatar editor or Settings → Bot to manage it. Appearance edits include the name and animated avatar. Behavior includes memory, initiative and check frequency. Some saved changes wait for an active reply to finish.

The mobile companion also offers your personal Bot in its sidebar when the device has access. It uses the same conversation, animated custom avatar, message bubbles and reactions. Tap its mobile header for status, watch information and Snooze/Wake up. Desktop remains the runtime and must be open and connected. Bot appearance, permissions and individual watch editing remain on desktop; private internal watch chats are not exposed to the companion.

## Conversation and browser

A successfully loaded browser or other host tool group can carry forward into the next foreground reply. Available actions are checked against current access settings; earlier plugin grants are not replayed. The browser card highlights its background on hover without showing a border.

In a narrow conversation pane, the name and avatar float over the messages with a soft shadow, leaving the conversation its full height. They remain visible in an empty chat. In a wide pane, a right-side Bot card shows its identity, Message and Edit bot controls, its browser, watches, recent tool activity and saved outputs when available. Opening the workspace returns the identity to the floating layout so the conversation keeps room. Recent activity links return to the relevant message in this Bot conversation; they are not separate delegated Work chats. Message focuses the composer in TinyGPT; phone, SMS, calls and Slack are not Bot contact channels in this interface.

Enable Browse the web in Bot access settings to allow browser/research tools, subject to shared permissions and approval checks. Foreground Bot turns can load the interactive browser group, including listing/reusing tabs, snapshots, click, type, scroll, hover and key actions. Active browser work has a live preview and Watch control; the browser card uses a browser illustration and opens the same workspace browser when clicked anywhere. Its compact surface highlights on hover, with Ready, Browsing, Off or Sleeping beneath the name. Interactive Bot tabs survive between replies while the app stays open, even if not watched. Quiet research tabs are still temporary. Restarting does not restore open tabs; persistent browser-profile cookies can keep a site signed in. Login and saved-password entry remain user-controlled. Private proactive checks have read-only browser access, including screenshots and image inspection, and cannot click through changes. Browser discovery identifies whether this turn is foreground or a proactive read-only check; a missing click action during a watch is an intentional restriction, not evidence that the app lacks interaction tools. Continue in the Bot conversation for interactive changes, subject to the normal permissions.

The Bot acts directly inside its ongoing chat. Private watch checks use their own internal Bot conversations and can deliver useful findings back to the main Bot chat. The Bot does not currently create or delegate user-facing Work chats, run shell commands, or use Work-only file/task tools. Its declared project file tools are separate from Work-only actions. The Bot uses the currently selected inference connection/model and shares Chat's effort setting; it has no independent Bot effort default. These are current capabilities, not a promise that a particular connected plugin exposes a needed action.

If a Bot message cannot finish, earlier delivered messages stay saved. The error notice can distinguish authentication, provider limits, temporary provider failures and a rejected conversation format. A repeating conversation-format error can be reported through Diagnostics; the diagnostic records a fixed category and HTTP status without copying the upstream error body. A stopped reply does not establish whether a requested account change succeeded: inspect the recorded tool results and saved messages before continuing.

## Snooze and wake

Choose Snooze in the wide Bot card or Snooze bot in the sidebar Bot menu. The sidebar and conversation avatars use the snooze animation and the status reads Sleeping. Snooze stops current Bot replies and private checks, blocks new Bot replies and pauses proactive checks and delivery until you explicitly wake the Bot. The conversation shows Wake bot in place of the composer; the card and sidebar menu also offer Wake. Sleep persists after restarting TinyGPT. Memory, permissions and individual watch pause settings are preserved. Your separate user-created Scheduled tasks continue normally. Due Bot watches can resume after waking; sleep does not run missed checks in a batch.

Keeping an eye on uses compact single-line watch rows with a clock icon with a three-dot menu with Pause (or Resume), Check now and Remove. Check now runs a private, read-only check immediately without changing the next scheduled check or resuming a paused watch. It is unavailable while the Bot is sleeping or already checking; if another task is using the runtime, wait for it to finish. Next-check timing appears in a styled tooltip when you hover or keyboard-focus the row, and at the top of its menu, rather than as a second line. Paused watches retain a small Paused label. Recent activity groups tool steps into up to five recent requests or proactive updates. Each row uses the original request or update text, links to its reply, and keeps a representative tool icon. Its tooltip shows reply status and the number of tool steps. These are display labels from existing messages, not another model-generated summary or evidence that a task succeeded. New requests enter at the top; additional steps update that request instead of filling the list. Motion preferences are respected. Hover or keyboard focus reveals the three-dot menu to open the reply and, for browser activity, the browser. These controls do not erase tool history.

## Manage Bot access

The Bot's plugin access controls refer to permission to use accounts in that conversation, not simply whether a plugin is installed. Turning access off prevents subsequent use and removes its grants; it cannot retract an action already dispatched. Account connections can remain available to other conversations. Newly selected plugin tools may become callable on the next message.

Bot memory and personal-memory sharing are distinct controls. Bot notes supply persistent personality, preferences and remembered context according to its configuration. Do not assume pausing a personal memory deletes Bot notes or original messages. Inspect Bot configuration when asking what it remembers.

In Settings → Bot, Remember useful details controls Bot memory; Browse the web controls browser/research use. Take initiative enables proactive work between 8 AM and 10 PM; Check in periodically offers Off, Every 30 minutes and Every hour. Save changes applies the access/behavior edits. Under Personalization, choose Personality, About you, Instructions or Notes, edit its text and select Save personalization. Treat these notes as private context; do not store credentials there.

## Proactive watches

Saving a watch schedules future checks; it does not perform the action described in its prompt. Repeated unchanged watch or memory saves temporarily remove that maintenance tool from the current reply so the Bot can return to the actual task. It becomes available again on the next reply. Productive writes and repeated observations are not a task-length limit. An identical watch prompt and interval reuse the saved watch even if a different title is proposed, and title matching ignores capitalization. Existing watches and user pauses are preserved.

When enabled, the Bot can perform private checks and maintain watches for interests or commitments. These watches are separate from the user-facing Scheduled list. Checks should report worthwhile developments rather than repeated generic messages. Autonomous checks cannot wait on an approval card and have restrictions on external messaging, purchases, edits and commands. Missing permission can prevent a watch from doing useful work.

Interest watches check at intervals of at least 30 minutes; they are not 5-minute reminders. Saving an identical watch does not reset its next check or resume a watch you paused. The general Personal check-in is managed by the user's check-frequency setting, not the Bot's interest-watch tool. The wide Bot card lets you pause or resume individual watches; initiative must also be on for checks to run.

Ask the Bot to stop watching a topic or to remove verification watches after the task is done. Its bot_watch_remove tool removes a specific Bot interest watch by the saved ID, including paused watches, and remains available in the conversation when initiative is off. A private proactive check may remove only its own interest watch after verifying its completion condition. It cannot remove a user-created Scheduled task, another watch during a private check, or the general Personal check-in. Successful removal stops future checks and updates Keeping an eye on; it preserves past conversations and run history. Retrying a removed ID reports that the watch is already absent. The Bot must check the tool result before claiming removal. Watch minutes are the recurring check interval, not an automatic expiry: a 30-minute watch does not disappear after 30 minutes.

## Schedule your own task

Open Scheduled, create a task and enter its prompt. Choose Once (date/time), Hourly, Daily, Weekdays or Weekly; Weekly also selects a day. The editor shows the timezone used for times. Advanced contains Name, Start each run in a new chat and Mode (Chat or Work). Tasks use the current model and selected plugins. Inspect the next run and run history; available task actions include running now, stopping, pausing/resuming and removing. Generated starter ideas are suggestions, not enabled tasks until saved. Scheduled work requires the desktop application and relevant connections to be available; do not assume a closed or sleeping computer runs jobs. Remote keep-awake prevents automatic sleep only while its configured conditions apply.

articles.title: Plugins, connected accounts, MCP and skills
articles.text:
# Plugins, connected accounts, MCP and skills

Open Settings → Plugins to manage integrations, accounts, selected knowledge, Skills and custom MCP servers. Plugins add tools for services such as mail, calendars, files and development systems. Available integrations depend on the catalog and configured connections; TinyGPT must not infer access just because a service name appears in a conversation.

## Connect an account

Choose the relevant plugin and follow its connection/sign-in flow. Complete authorization in the supplied browser or dialog. Select or permit its use in the intended conversation when requested. Connecting an account, granting conversation read access and approving an action are separate steps. An installed plugin with no working account connection cannot read that account.

For an account task, ask the assistant to discover the relevant service tools and use actual results. Reconnect if authorization has expired or been revoked. Revoking access prevents future use but cannot undo previously completed external actions. Removing an account from one chat does not necessarily disconnect it everywhere.

A focused plugin search loads only matching action schemas. It also supplies a bounded, schema-free index of actions in those connected plugins, with a count and completeness indicator. A search-only selection does not mean the entire plugin only supports search. Other actions must be loaded explicitly and still follow account scopes, conversation access and action approvals. Discovery does not execute those actions.

In local OpenAI-compatible Work runs, discovered action parameters are returned as data and the assistant calls them through a fixed invoke_tool interface. This keeps the callable tool definitions stable for prompt cache reuse. An action must belong to the run's captured plugin catalog and be explicitly loaded; current host validation, account access and approvals still apply. Chat, Bot and other protocols keep their existing loading interface.

The built-in Gmail connector supports account lookup, message search and reading, plus sending when separately authorized. It currently has no tools to create Gmail filters, archive mail or mark messages read. Connecting Gmail does not provide a signed-in Gmail browser session. Such unsupported settings actions may require the Gmail website and a separate browser sign-in; do not assume an OAuth connection grants browser cookies or additional Gmail permissions.

## Add custom tools

Use the MCP tab to configure a supported server, transport and authentication. Only use commands/endpoints you intend to trust. A server can expose tools and resources; their availability does not grant permission to execute a consequential action. Protect credentials and do not paste them into ordinary chat or bundled documentation.

## Use skills

The Skills tab manages installed procedural guidance and the skills library. Select a relevant skill or ask the assistant to find one. A skill can provide instructions and resources for a task; it does not create a missing account connection or override denied tool permissions. Reading a skill is different from executing the programs or actions it describes.

articles.title: Browser and computer control
articles.text:
# Browser and computer control

Inline questions, tool approvals and sign-in handoff cards are conversation regions, not modal overlays. They leave the workspace browser live and interactive so you can browse or complete a sign-in while Work waits. A true app dialog or open overlay temporarily covers the native page with a non-interactive preview; closing it restores the live page. Resizing the workspace similarly uses a temporary preview and restores interaction when resizing ends. A preview image itself cannot accept page clicks.

TinyGPT can research web pages and, when enabled and authorized, interact with websites or supported desktop windows. These are different access categories. A website login does not grant desktop control, and desktop access does not grant account API access.

## Browser tasks

Ask for a website task and allow the necessary reading/interaction permissions. TinyGPT uses current page observations and labeled controls. A stale tab or changed page may require a fresh snapshot. When a page requests sign-in, consent or verification, complete the handoff in the same tab. Do not provide passwords through ordinary chat. The assistant should verify a success state after submission rather than repeating a click because a response is delayed.

Browser snapshots focus on the open modal dialog by default. Filters search that collected scope before pagination; an explicit page-wide scope can inspect background controls, which may still be covered and cannot be clicked through. A blocked-control result distinguishes an overlay from an expired reference, provides a fresh observation when reading is authorized, and never closes a dialog or repeats the click automatically. Text coverage identifies whether it describes dialog, main-content or page text; a complete excerpt does not prove every DOM node was read. Accessibility-outline truncation is reported separately.

Observed web links include safe HTTP(S) destinations when they fit the response budget. Pages expose their observed HTTP status and identify authentication-required, forbidden, not-found and server-error responses. Successfully reading an error page is not successful completion of the website task. Browser sign-in cookies do not establish API authorization.

With image interpretation available, loading browser tools also offers view_image alongside screenshot capture. Capturing a screenshot saves an immutable image reference; it does not inspect its pixels. Use the returned image-reader call rather than passing the reference to the text-file reader or capturing the whole desktop. Image interpretation and browser/desktop permissions remain separate. Saved page sources and archived observations return reader-call hints; a source ID belongs to read_source, while an observation ID belongs to read_observation. Neither is a Project file path.

Settings → Browser chooses the default search engine, web and local link destinations, full URL display and TinyGPT AdBlock. Reload pages after changing blocking. AdBlock blocks common ad/tracking requests; it is not a guarantee against every tracker. Browsing data can clear history, cookies, site data and cache across shared/isolated Project profiles. Downloaded files and saved chat sources remain.

## Saved passwords and private sign-in

On an HTTPS page in the main workspace browser, choose **Passwords** (the lock icon beside the address). Opening private sign-in stops active assistant replies and command jobs first; tools across chats stay paused until the private window closes. Due Scheduled tasks wait until private sign-in is finished. You can continue your chat afterward. Enter the username and password in this separate trusted window, choose **Save**, then select the saved account and **Fill password**. **Generate** creates a random 24-character password. Existing accounts require confirmation before an update or removal. TinyGPT does not automatically capture passwords typed into websites or import passwords from other browsers.

Windows stores these credentials in Windows Credential Manager and requires Windows Hello approval for every fill. Hello must be available; there is no unprotected fallback. Windows account protection is different from a cryptographically Hello-bound vault: other programs or unrestricted commands running as your Windows user remain outside this protection. The macOS backend uses Data Protection Keychain items requiring user presence, with Touch ID or system authentication; the build must contain the native service and have the necessary signing/Keychain identity. Missing native services or failed protection stop the request.

Accounts match the exact HTTPS origin (including its port) and browser profile. An isolated Project does not inherit the shared profile’s saved passwords. Filling supports a visible, unambiguous, main-page sign-in form that submits to the same origin with POST. It rejects invisible fields, cross-origin submissions, iframe-only forms, new-password forms and forms changed during authentication. Unsupported forms need manual interaction in the private window. The current website origin appears in the private window; check it before signing in.

Submit the website’s form yourself, then choose **Finish sign-in**. TinyGPT destroys the private page and opens the original site’s home page using the shared signed-in session. It does not repeat a submission or claim authentication succeeded. **Close** ends private mode without navigating the normal tab. The window closes on OS lock, sleep, app exit, or after five minutes. Clearing browsing data signs sites out but does not delete saved passwords; remove each saved account separately.

The password feature has no model-facing password read or fill tool. Password values do not enter chats, memory, sources, tool results or previews through this feature. The private page has no agent connection, no saved browsing history and no download access. App-owned desktop tools and browser captures are blocked while it is open; remote-debugging sessions cannot open it. The intended website receives a filled password, and its scripts can see or echo it. This is not a guarantee against malicious websites, unrestricted same-user programs/commands, or a compromised operating system. Do not put passwords into chat.

## Desktop tasks

Image inspection preserves the requested visual question, including on text-heavy screenshots. OCR text is supplemental evidence; it does not identify checked states by itself. Bounded textRegions boxes use original-image coordinates and prioritize question matches to help choose grounded crops. These text boxes are not clickable browser targets. A short completed visual answer does not trigger an automatic crop just for being short. Results remain partial and fallible; use live browser selected/checked state when available.

Open Settings → Computer use, enable Computer tools in Chat if wanted, and check Local computer runtime. macOS may require Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions. Approve the intended window and action. Reading accessible text and controlling a window have separate approvals; consequential actions need their own authorization. Availability varies by platform, app accessibility and installed runtime.

Use Stop computer use to stop desktop actions across chats, and resume only when intended. Current accessible labels and screenshots are evidence; the assistant must not invent window/control identifiers or claim an unseen outcome. Approval does not make a fallible model's visual interpretation reliable. When a control cannot be read, ask for a supported alternative or clarify the state.

articles.title: Voice, images and media
articles.text:
# Voice, images and media

Settings → Voice configures dictation and read aloud. These are separate from a model's ability to understand images or generate new images. A feature's presence in the interface does not establish that its runtime or provider is ready.

## Dictate a message

Choose the microphone, allow operating-system microphone access if requested, and use the composer microphone control. Bundled transcription turns speech into a draft on this computer; review the draft before sending. Microphone audio for bundled transcription stays local. Once sent, the resulting text goes to the selected inference connection. Transcription language is English in this interface. The speech model supplies punctuation/capitalization and manages phrase boundaries; noise reduction and echo reduction are configurable.

## Read an answer aloud

Enable Read aloud, choose Speech model and Voice, adjust Playback speed and use Try this voice. Completed answers expose read-aloud playback when enabled. Bundled speech and a connected speech provider have different data flows. A connected provider can receive the text to speak. Voice customization, where offered by the selected model, follows that setup flow; inspect its status rather than assuming all providers support the same voices.

## Understand or create an image

Attach an image and ask a focused question. Depending on the connection, image tools may use the selected vision model or a local helper. Extracted text and visual interpretation are different evidence; small labels, charts and measurements may need a focused crop or closer inspection. The assistant must acknowledge unreadable or omitted details.

Image generation requires an available configured image-generation connection/model and any applicable approval. Provider charges and network access can apply. Generated images are outputs, not proof of real-world facts. Do not assume that image support implies video generation or that every image format/export is available.

articles.title: Remote Control and paired devices
articles.text:
# Remote Control and paired devices

Settings → Remote Control lets paired devices access shared chats while the desktop application is open. Your computer must remain connected and available. Remote access is not an independent cloud copy that can keep working after the desktop is closed.

## Pair a device

Open Paired devices, choose Add device and follow the QR-code pairing flow on the intended device. Treat pairing information as access information. Confirm the device and choose its conversation access. The companion interface provides supported chat, attachment, model, queue, notification and settings views; desktop and mobile controls need not be identical.

## Read Chat and Work on a phone

The companion uses the desktop message components. Chat shows one tool chain with a single replaceable progress message below it, followed by the final answer. Progress disappears when the harness identifies the answer; model-specific answer validation still applies.

Generated UI answers, including tables, charts, checklists and suggested follow-up questions, also appear on mobile. A visual answer hides temporary progress as soon as it begins. The companion uses the same tool icons as desktop, including mapped plugin icons. Follow-up buttons fill the message composer for review; they do not send a message automatically. Preview visuals remain non-interactive until completed.

Generated visuals are fetched separately through the encrypted, paired connection for an authorized conversation. Only validated display components are returned, without the raw tool result. Mobile retains references for up to 96 recent visuals in its recent message window; older visuals remain available on desktop. This does not grant account, file or browser control beyond the device's existing permissions.

Work shows chronological prose and tool activity, with delegated coding inside an inline **Coding agent** section. The section opens while its coding call is active and collapses when that call ends. The outer Work history stays open until the assistant’s answer is confirmed, then collapses; tap it to review retained activity. A completed coding call alone does not mark the whole task complete.

Mobile receives a bounded recent display rather than the desktop’s full native session. Retained child tools keep their Coding agent parent and ownership, even when the parent is older than the ordinary recent-tool window. Long notes are truncated with the existing omission indication; full history remains on the computer. This does not grant file access or add raw tool results or full command output to the companion. File targets in tool display metadata are reduced to file names. Available message actions and approvals still depend on the paired device’s access.

## Talk to your Bot on mobile

After setting up your Bot on desktop, open the companion sidebar and tap its name and animated avatar. The Bot name aligns with New chat, and its animated avatar occupies the same icon column and visual size. Devices with conversation-library access can see your personal Bot. A device paired to just one ordinary chat does not gain Bot access; pairing directly to the personal Bot shares only that conversation. The same persistent Bot conversation, custom avatar, message bubbles, reactions and incoming messages appear on phone and desktop. This does not create a separate mobile Bot or move its runtime to the phone.

Tap the Bot name/avatar above the messages to open its information sheet, with its status, browser availability and Keeping an eye on watch titles and next-check times. Snooze and Wake up control the same saved sleeping state as desktop: sleeping stops replies and proactive work until you wake it. The animation and composer reflect sleeping on both devices. Individual watch management, Bot appearance editing, memory/permissions setup and watching or controlling its workspace browser remain on desktop. The browser availability shown on mobile is not a remote browser-control surface.

Main Bot messages can appear in companion notifications and paired-device push notifications according to notification preferences. Only the configured personal Bot is shared; private internal watch conversations, their prompts, raw results, memory notes and plugin grants are not added to the mobile library. Normal conversation-scoped device restrictions and revocation still apply. Your desktop must stay open and connected for Bot replies or proactive messages to reach the phone.

## Limit or revoke access

Use Paired devices to change shared conversation access or revoke an individual device. Allow remote connections turns availability on or off while preserving saved paired devices. Remove all remote access forgets every paired device; each will need a new QR code to reconnect. Revocation prevents later access and cannot retract information already viewed by a device.

Keep this computer awake prevents automatic system sleep while remote connections are allowed; the display can still turn off. It does not prevent shutdown, lost internet or application failure. Check Connection status when the companion cannot connect, then confirm the desktop is open, remote access is enabled and the device is still paired.

Remote transport uses the configured relay and device pairing/cryptography. This does not change the selected model's privacy behavior: cloud inference still receives prompts and relevant context. Notification previews can reveal information on a device's screen; review both TinyGPT and device notification settings.

The main website at https://tinygpt.org/downloads includes a **Remote Control** link below the desktop installers. It opens https://mobile.tinygpt.org, where you can install the mobile web app or continue in the browser. A running desktop app and approved pairing are still required; this is not independent hosted inference.

articles.title: Privacy, permissions and data deletion
articles.text:
# Privacy, permissions and data deletion

TinyGPT stores conversations, Projects, preferences, saved memories and indexes on this computer. Local storage is separate from inference processing. When a cloud inference connection is selected, prompts and relevant context, including retrieved excerpts or attachments, can be sent to that connection. Web tools contact websites, plugins contact their services, and remote access shares permitted information with paired devices.

## Choose privacy controls

In Configuration → OpenRouter, Zero data retention restricts eligible providers and Allow data collection controls collection eligibility. These are routing policies for that connection; they do not prove that every external service or plugin uses the same policy. Use a ready local model for local inference, and consider the separate network effects of tools used in a task.

Settings → General contains tool approvals for reading files/saved sources, changing files, running commands, searching/reading pages, interacting with websites, reading/controlling desktop windows, sending messages and purchases. Choose Ask me first, allow automatically or never allow as appropriate. Approval may be scoped to an action, run or conversation. Never allow remains a boundary; loading tools or skills does not bypass it.

New profiles allow file/saved-source reading by default and ask before writes, commands, browser access/interaction, desktop reads/control, sending and purchases. Existing saved choices can differ; inspect your current controls. Bundled help reads only application documentation and does not require permission to read your personal files.

## Remove information deliberately

Archiving hides a chat; it does not delete it. Forgetting memories/indexes removes retrieval evidence and derived checkpoints while original files/messages remain. Disabling personal-memory sharing prevents eligible future sharing but does not recall text already sent to providers. Clearing browser data removes browser storage; downloads and saved chat sources remain. Revoking a plugin or remote device blocks future access, not past external effects. Use the corresponding controls for each kind of information you want removed.

## Credentials and diagnostics

Provider credentials use the app's protected credential storage where supported. Do not put keys in prompts, memory or generated documentation. Settings → Diagnostics records local reply timing/status when enabled; its records exclude conversation text, files, credentials, URLs and paths and are not automatically uploaded. Review an export before sharing it. Operating-system/device access and any manually exported files have their own privacy boundaries.

During active local runs, Diagnostics can also record numeric GPU load, memory, clocks, power, temperature, limiting states, host-memory availability and counts of app-owned/other compute processes. Process names, command lines, process IDs and GPU UUIDs are not saved. NVIDIA counters require a working local nvidia-smi; unsupported readings remain unavailable. App-managed runtime records include numeric output rates, acceleration acceptance, snapshot budgets and skipped snapshots. Disabling Diagnostics or clearing records stops hardware sampling and discards late results. Existing seven-day/200-run retention applies; no hardware telemetry is automatically uploaded.

The workspace browser’s **Passwords** control opens private sign-in. Saved website passwords use a separate OS credential store; account labels use an encrypted local index. The feature does not return passwords to model tools, chats, memory, sources or previews. Active replies stop and assistant tools pause before credential entry. Fill requires user action and OS authentication, is bound to the exact HTTPS origin and browser profile, and never submits the website’s form automatically. Finish closes the private page before normal browsing continues with the signed-in session. Closing, OS lock/sleep or a five-minute timeout closes the private window. Passwords are removed separately from cookies/browsing data.

This boundary does not make passwords invisible to the website receiving them, nor protect against a compromised OS or unrestricted same-user commands. Windows Credential Manager is protected by the Windows account; TinyGPT’s per-fill Hello approval is not cryptographic protection against another program using that account. macOS Keychain user-presence protection requires a native build and suitable signed app identity. There is no plaintext or unprotected fallback. See the Browser and computer control article for the supported form types and sign-in steps.

articles.title: Appearance, profile and notifications
articles.text:
# Appearance, profile and notifications

Open Settings → Appearance to choose system, light or dark appearance and edit each theme's accent, background, foreground, contrast and translucency. Separate UI, content and code font settings control their typeface/weight; size and smoothing controls affect readability. Use Reduce motion to reduce animations or follow the system preference. Pointer cursors, app icon and diff markers have their own controls. Theme import/copy controls exchange supported TinyGPT theme JSON, not arbitrary executable themes.

## Change your profile

Open Settings → Profile, choose Edit, change first/last name or photo and save. The profile is local. A supplied name is also stored as a personal memory; control its availability in Personalization. Removing a photo and changing a name are separate operations. Profile activity panels show locally recorded usage such as token activity and most-used tools; they are not a provider billing invoice.

## Control notifications

Open Settings → Notifications. Pause alerts silences alerts and sounds while Activity continues updating. Choose desktop notifications, whether to notify only when away, message previews and unread dots. Individual event types include Chat replies, Work tasks, Bot replies/jobs, attention requests and problems/interruptions.

Enable sound, choose the TinyGPT chime or a supported custom WAV/MP3, set volume and preview it. Quiet hours pause alerts/sounds during the selected local-time interval. Test desktop notification checks delivery, but operating-system notification settings or focus modes may still suppress it. Message previews can expose a title and text on the screen; disable them if that is unwanted.

The Activity feed and unread indicators help find completed work or requests for attention. A notification is not independent proof of the correctness of a task's result; inspect its conversation, tool results and output files.

Each newly saved Bot message creates its own notification event, including messages sent while the Bot continues working and proactive updates. Empty typing placeholders do not notify, repeated updates do not duplicate a message, and finishing the run does not add an extra completion alert for the same message. Historical messages are not replayed as desktop alerts after restarting or dismissing notifications. Desktop alerts, paired-device delivery, quiet hours, away-only preferences and sound limits still apply. Chat and Work completion notifications remain per run.

articles.title: Troubleshooting and current limitations
articles.text:
# Troubleshooting and current limitations

When a feature fails, inspect the displayed error/status and the actual tool result. Do not repeatedly submit a consequential action without checking whether it already happened. Stop interrupts work where supported; it does not undo completed edits, messages or purchases.

## A model will not answer

Open Configuration and inspect the selected connection, model readiness, credentials and device/memory status. Local servers must be running; optional assets may need installation. Cloud providers need a working network/account and may apply limits or charges. Try a supported model/connection and report the exact error without including keys. Effort, tool use and vision depend on model support.

## A tool or account is unavailable

Check General permissions, relevant runtime settings and the plugin's connection and conversation access. A model may need to load the appropriate tool group before an action is callable. A missing tool or denied action is not permission to use another path. Sign-in/verification requires the user's handoff. Account access cannot be inferred from older conversation claims.

## A file or memory cannot be found

Check the Project, attachment processing state, personal-memory sharing, folder-index status and read permissions. Refresh an eligible index after changes. Inspect retrieval to see actual evidence. Keyword search can still work while local semantic inference recovers. The assistant does not have unrestricted access to every disk file, unrelated Project or prior chat.

## Replies are slow

Inspect Configuration memory and model residency; loading a cold model, long prompts and large tasks take time. Enable Record reply diagnostics in Settings → Diagnostics to inspect recent timing/status, export a report or clear records. Records have retention limits and are pruned at startup/read. Diagnostics do not establish a hardware-independent performance guarantee.

## Limits to remember

Help describes the installed build, not every roadmap item. Model answers, vision and generated content can be wrong. Local features do not make cloud tools offline. File processing has format/size limits; a failed extraction must be reported. Running commands is not a general OS sandbox. Remote/scheduled features depend on the available desktop and connections. A connection to another product's consumer subscription is not automatically a supported inference integration. Ask the assistant to check current tools and status before promising an action.

articles.title: Updating TinyGPT and keeping local models
articles.text:
# Updating TinyGPT and keeping local models

Signed Windows x64 release builds can check the TinyGPT pre-beta update channel. Unsigned builds, development sessions and Mac builds do not enable this updater. The previously published 0.1.0-prebeta.2 build does not contain an updater; install an updater-enabled release manually once before expecting update notifications.

## Check, download and restart

Open **Settings → General → Updates → Check for updates**. A supported build also checks on startup and every four hours while running. When a newer version is found, **Update available** appears above the sidebar profile. Open it to read plain-text release notes and choose **Download update**. Downloads are not started merely because an update is available. Progress appears in the sidebar and update panel. You can keep using the app during a download.

After a verified download, choose **Restart to update**. The app refuses to restart through this control while Chat, Work, Bot or Scheduled work is active or a workspace terminal is still open. Finish the work and close terminals, then try again. Updates do not install automatically just because you quit the app. Download/check failures provide a retry through checking again; a failed check is not proof that you have the latest version.

Windows updates verify the expected publisher's code signature and package checksum. Builds with no configured publisher disable in-app updating rather than accept unsigned replacements. Update metadata and files come from downloads.tinygpt.org over HTTPS; the app checks that release artifact locations stay on that host. Update checks and model downloads expose ordinary network metadata to the hosting service. The updater's per-installation staging identifier header is suppressed. Chats, memories, profile names, API keys and account credentials are not supplied to the updater.

## Smaller app downloads

The app updater uses package block maps and HTTP byte ranges to reuse unchanged blocks from its local update cache. It reconstructs a complete package locally and verifies it before installation. This reduces network transfer when blocks match; it does not eliminate temporary disk-space requirements. Missing or incompatible update caches, or changed compression/package layout, can require downloading the complete app package. A small source edit does not guarantee a particular update size.

## Models are kept separately

New installer builds separate app files from approximately 2.48 GB of included local model data. First launch prepares the model files in a separate local-profile model store, showing progress and downloading only missing, changed or corrupt model objects. Matching model files from a previous installation can be retained by the installer before it removes the old app. Each downloaded file is checked against the size and SHA-256 pinned in the release's model catalog; incomplete downloads can resume on a later launch. Closing the model setup window cancels setup. If setup fails, reopen TinyGPT to continue. Setup needs internet when required files are not already available locally.

The verified models stay across app updates. An app-package fallback download does not normally require downloading unchanged models again. A complete prepared installation can use included local AI and voice offline; optional external providers and online tools still need their own connectivity. This local model store is separate from personal memories and Project indexing. Forgetting personal memories does not clear model weights, and there is no model-cache cleanup button in Personalization. Versioned resource views and update reconstruction can use additional disk space.

Code signing, identity verification and SmartScreen reputation are separate from the illustrated installer. A new signed publisher can still receive a Windows reputation warning. Product help describes the intended release behavior; the installed build's update status establishes whether updates are actually available. Mac pre-beta downloads and Mac updating are not part of the current Windows release pipeline.

articles.title: Settings: General
articles.text:
# Settings: General
